rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act: violations (Bus. & Prof. Code 16729, 16756.1)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any methodology used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term.
rules.penalty: Violation of the Cartwright Act is punishable as a crime (per the digest); no specific penalty is stated in the new sections.
rules.citation: Assembly Bill No. 325, Chapter 338; Business and Professions Code Section 16729
rules.status_basis: Approved by Governor October 06, 2025; chaptered as Chapter 338. Effective date not stated in the text.

coverage.summary: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, not limited to housing.

precedence.text: Nothing in this section shall impair or limit the applicability of antitrust laws.

rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
